rules.when: The issue has the label modell:text, or the task writes docs, pitch scripts, or copy against an agreed plan. Unclear product decisions still use modell:schwer.
rules.why: Use a cheap model for specified writing tasks.

rules.when: The issue has the label modell:klein, or the task is a small, fully specified change in one or two files with a direct pass/fail check.
rules.why: Cheapest fast model for easy work.

rules.when: The issue has the label modell:ui, or the task is user-facing UI: screens, components, layout, styling, or animation that the judges see in the demo.
rules.why: The UI is what people see in the demo, so it gets the strongest model.

rules.when: The issue has the label modell:schwer, or the task is hard or unclear: architecture, a risky multi-file change, the shared API contract, or planning.
rules.why: Unclear work needs the most reasoning. The list lets firstmate use whichever plan has quota left.

rules.when: The issue has the label modell:bugfix, or the task is a bug fix with a known cause, or code against an existing spec or failing test.
rules.why: Once the problem is clear, a mid-tier model is enough.

rules.when: The issue has the label modell:recherche, or the task is research or reading only: partner briefings, API or library docs, datasets, or past hackathon winners, with a written report as the result.
rules.why: Reading-heavy scout work goes to Codex and keeps Claude quota for UI and hard code.
